title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Lawfully Conducting Trial Work during Earthquake Relief and Post-Disaster Reconstruction in the Yushu Area of Qinghai Province and Effectively Maintaining Social Stability in the Disaster-Stricken Areas
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Lawfully Conducting Trial Work During Earthquake Relief and Post-Disaster Reconstruction in the Yushu Region of Qinghai Province and Effectively Maintaining Social Stability in the Disaster Area

Fa [2010] No. 178

To: Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The extraordinarily severe earthquake disaster that occurred in the Yushu region of Qinghai Province has caused enormous losses to the lives and property of the people in the disaster area and has severely disrupted production and daily life in the affected region. Under the strong leadership and meticulous planning of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council, earthquake relief efforts have achieved interim results, and post-disaster reconstruction work is about to commence. During the period of earthquake relief and post-disaster reconstruction, people's courts at all levels nationwide must adhere to the leadership of the Party, fully leverage the adjudicative functions of the people's courts, focus on maintaining social stability, resolving conflicts, and promoting harmony, so as to provide strong judicial guarantees and services for earthquake relief and post-disaster reconstruction, and make due contributions to achieving a comprehensive victory in earthquake relief and ensuring the smooth progress of post-disaster reconstruction. To conduct current trial work effectively and maintain social stability in the disaster area, the following matters are hereby notified:

1. People's courts at all levels must thoroughly comprehend the series of arrangements made by the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council regarding earthquake relief work and the important directives of General Secretary Hu Jintao, regarding earthquake relief as the most urgent and important task at present. The trial and enforcement of cases related to the extraordinarily severe earthquake disaster in the Yushu region of Qinghai Province must proceed from the overall situation, be conducive to maintaining social stability, be conducive to safeguarding the fundamental interests of the broadest majority of the people, be conducive to strengthening ethnic unity, and be conducive to consolidating the achievements of earthquake relief and ensuring the smooth progress of post-disaster reconstruction. We must carefully study and accurately apply laws, administrative regulations, and judicial interpretations related to disaster-related cases, such as the Earthquake Prevention and Disaster Reduction Law, the Emergency Response Law, etc., and, in light of the current realities of earthquake relief work, strengthen overall coordination to provide strong judicial guarantees for earthquake relief and post-disaster reconstruction, effectively maintain public order in the disaster area, and enhance the sense of security among the people in the disaster area.

2. Lawfully and severely punish various criminal activities that endanger earthquake relief and post-disaster reconstruction, and resolutely maintain social stability in the disaster area. People's courts must lawfully protect the lives and property of the people in the disaster area, and severely crack down on illegal and criminal acts that intentionally undermine stability in the disaster area, harm the achievements of earthquake relief, hinder the smooth progress of post-disaster reconstruction, and affect the confidence and determination of the people in the disaster area to rebuild their homes.

Adhere to the policy of special handling for special periods and special cases, and for criminal acts that seriously endanger the progress of earthquake relief and post-disaster reconstruction, conduct speedy trials and render speedy judgments within the statutory time limit, striving to make the people in the disaster area feel the determination and strength of the people's courts in maintaining stability in the disaster area and combating crime within the shortest possible time, deterring potential criminals, and preventing the occurrence of other crimes.

Strictly implement the criminal policy of combining leniency with severity, pay attention to distinguishing between different natures of illegal and criminal acts, demonstrate judicial authority, and provide strong judicial guarantees for the production and daily life of the disaster area in a way visible and perceptible to the people.

3. The following criminal acts occurring during the period of earthquake relief and post-disaster reconstruction shall be given heavier punishment in accordance with law:

(1) Criminal acts such as theft, robbery, pillaging, intentional destruction of materials, equipment, and facilities used for earthquake relief; fraud or extortion of money under the guise of disaster relief fundraising; trafficking of orphaned or disabled children and women in the disaster area.

(2) Criminal acts such as hoarding and profiteering, price gouging, illegal business operations, and forced transactions for the purpose of seeking exorbitant profits, which seriously disrupt market order in the disaster area and affect the normal production and daily life of the people in the disaster area.

(3) Criminal acts such as intentionally fabricating, disseminating, or spreading false or terroristic information that is detrimental to the stability of the disaster area, endangering ethnic unity, and seriously affecting the development of earthquake relief and post-disaster reconstruction; obstructing official duties; gathering crowds to disturb social order, public place order, or traffic order; and gathering crowds to assault state organs.

(4) Criminal acts such as producing or selling substandard products, toxic or harmful food, or counterfeit or inferior drugs in the disaster area, or intentionally providing such items to the disaster area under the guise of disaster relief.

(5) Criminal acts by state functionaries such as embezzling or misappropriating earthquake relief funds and materials, abusing their power, or neglecting their duties, thereby endangering the smooth progress of earthquake relief and post-disaster reconstruction and seriously damaging the image of the Party and the state.

(6) Criminal acts of damaging public facilities such as electricity, transportation, and telecommunications.

(7) Criminal acts endangering public health, such as obstructing the prevention and control of infectious diseases.

4. People's courts in the disaster area must, under the unified leadership of the Party committee, promptly resolve various disputes and conflicts arising during earthquake relief and post-disaster reconstruction, encourage and support organizations such as people's mediation in resolving disputes, and actively support administrative organs in using administrative means to resolve disputes. For civil and other cases filed with the people's court, different situations shall be handled separately: for cases involving the basic livelihood security of the disaster area population or the restoration of production and daily life, cases shall be promptly filed, tried, and enforced in accordance with law; for cases that may affect the smooth progress of earthquake relief and post-disaster reconstruction, or that are group-related or socially sensitive, coordination with relevant departments shall be actively undertaken, and careful examination of case filing shall be conducted. During the trial process, particular attention shall be paid to pre-litigation mediation, and efforts shall be made to mediate between the parties, resolving disputes as far as possible through mediation or withdrawal upon reconciliation, effectively achieving the goal of "case concluded and matters settled." During trial and enforcement, special attention shall be paid to protecting the legitimate civil rights and interests of minors, elderly persons living alone, and persons disabled by the earthquake in the disaster area. We shall proactively introduce measures to facilitate and benefit the people, increase the intensity of judicial assistance, expand the scope of judicial assistance for the disaster-stricken population in the earthquake area, establish a green channel for judicial assistance in earthquake relief, simplify acceptance procedures, and strive to provide assistance to all who are eligible.

5. People's courts in the disaster area shall actively support and assist government departments in carrying out administrative resettlement, consolation, subsidies, relief, and other work. For conflicts and disputes arising during such work, people's courts shall proactively study the issues from a legal perspective and proactively propose recommendations and countermeasures for law-based administration and dispute resolution. In particular, under the unified leadership of the local Party committee, the roles of people's mediation, administrative mediation, and judicial mediation shall be fully utilized to form a three-in-one comprehensive dispute resolution mechanism, resolving conflicts at the source and reducing disputes.

6. During the period of post-disaster reconstruction, for cases filed by parties with the people's court that meet the conditions for case acceptance, especially cases involving declarations of missing persons or declarations of death, acceptance shall be timely to effectively guarantee the realization of the parties' right of action. For victims relocated to other places or taking refuge with relatives, who subsequently initiate lawsuits with the people's court due to disputes, since their current residence has changed, regarding jurisdiction, the Higher People's Court of Qinghai Province shall make overall arrangements in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law and other legal provisions, based on the principles of convenience for victims and stability. For disputes falling within the scope of case acceptance by the people's court, after accepting the case, the people's court shall effectively strengthen litigation guidance and legal clarification for disaster-related civil cases, and pay attention to alerting parties to litigation risks; for disputes that are not within or are unsuitable for handling by the people's court, efforts shall be made to carefully guide the parties' thinking, directing them to choose other effective channels and methods to resolve the disputes.

7. If a party is unable to assert rights in a timely manner due to force majeure caused by the extraordinarily severe earthquake disaster in Yushu, Qinghai, the statute of limitations shall be suspended in accordance with the provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law. The period of limitation shall continue to run from the date when the cause for suspension ceases to exist. If a party is unable to participate in litigation activities due to earthquake relief or post-disaster reconstruction, the people's court shall postpone or suspend the trial in accordance with law; after the cause for postponement or suspension ceases to exist, the trial shall be promptly resumed.

8. For cases of applications for declaring a person missing or declaring a person dead due to disappearance during the earthquake, people's courts shall actively accept such applications in accordance with law to clarify personal status and property relations as soon as possible. Since the grassroots people's court in the Yushu region has been severely damaged by the earthquake, if it is indeed difficult to exercise jurisdiction, the superior people's court may, in accordance with the provisions of Article 37, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law, designate another grassroots people's court to exercise jurisdiction.

9. For situations where people's courts in the disaster area are temporarily unable to conduct trial activities, the Higher People's Court of Qinghai Province shall coordinate uniformly and, in accordance with the relevant provisions of procedural law, strengthen the use of transfer of jurisdiction, designation of jurisdiction, and elevation of jurisdiction. Cases that have been accepted or are pending acceptance by the people's court in the disaster area and are suitable for trial by another people's court shall be transferred to or designated to another people's court for trial, or shall be directly taken up for trial or enforcement by a higher people's court.

10. In enforcement work, people's courts shall exercise caution in using compulsory enforcement measures. In particular, for funds and materials clearly designated for earthquake relief, property preservation measures and compulsory enforcement measures such as seizure, attachment, freezing, and transfer shall not be taken.

11. During the earthquake relief period, people's courts shall, in conjunction with the trial work of related cases, strengthen legal publicity, patiently provide psychological comfort and ideological guidance to the disaster-stricken population, especially the families of the deceased, and assist in the resettlement of the disaster-stricken population. Efforts shall be made to expand the social effect of trials, creating a favorable legal atmosphere for earthquake relief and post-disaster reconstruction. Together with relevant departments, comprehensive investigations shall be conducted, and conflicts and disputes during the post-disaster reconstruction process shall be promptly resolved.

12. Based on the actual circumstances and characteristics of local civil disputes, people's courts in the disaster area shall proactively make judicial suggestions to relevant departments regarding the protection of the legitimate civil rights and interests of the people, offering suggestions and countermeasures for relevant departments to take effective measures in an orderly and lawful manner.

13. For cases related to the earthquake in the Yushu region, people's courts may refer to the Supreme People's Court's Opinion on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Cases Related to the Wenchuan Earthquake (I) and the Supreme People's Court's Opinion on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Cases Related to the Wenchuan Earthquake (II) for handling. If new issues concerning the application of law arise during trial work, they shall be promptly reported to the Higher People's Court of Qinghai Province; major issues concerning the application of law shall be promptly reported level by level to the Supreme People's Court.

This notice is hereby given.

April 19, 2010
